To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“organizational factors play the most significant role in determining the overall success of a business intelligence system implementation”.
organizational factors play a crucial role in determining success of BI system implementation.
organizational factors play an important role in determining the CSFs for BI implementation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the CSFs and contextual factors in BI systems implementation.
the understanding of CSFs for implementing BI systems.
the CSFs for BI system implementation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the success of a business intelligence system depends on how well the organization manages its people, process, technology and data.
the organizational factors are the most crucial CSFs for BI implementation.
the organizational factors play the crucial role in determining success of BI system implementation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CSF framework of Yeoh and Korinios (2010) is applicable to the BI implementation domain, and that organizational factors are the most crucial CSFs in BI implementations.
our study extends the understanding of the CSF framework in the BI domain.
the CSFs are not independent and interdependent in nature, and the success of a CSF is contingent on the other factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the organizational context is the most critical dimension for successful BI implementation.
the CSFs are not static and they are context dependent.
the CSFs for BI systems implementation are not unique to a single organization.
